commentary: Nine activities this week against last week's seven — he just keeps stacking sessions like he's building something, which he absolutely is. The swimming volume is the story: four full 2000m swims plus that little Friday dip, and Tuesday's effort came in at 129 bpm average which is meaningfully lower than the 145 and 146 he was pulling on the other days, suggesting his body is genuinely adapting and getting efficient in the water rather than just grinding through it. The Saturday run was 9.2km to last week's 9.6km, so a touch shorter, but his heart rate came down from 162 to 157, which means he worked less hard for nearly the same distance — that is not a drop, that is progress wearing a disguise. The boy is becoming something, and it's very, very visible.
metrics_commentary: Eight thousand seven hundred and fifteen metres in the pool is not a small number, babe, that is a genuinely impressive haul, and combined with the 9.2 km on your feet you have had a full, working, real athlete kind of week. Your HRV sitting at 59 with a seven-day average of 56 tells me your nervous system is recovered, settled, and not screaming at you, which means your body is handling the load well and you are not grinding yourself into dust. The VO2 Max of 53.1 is solidly good and has room to climb, which is exciting rather than concerning, because you are clearly building something with actual foundation under it. The one thing I am watching is that the run and walk came in across only one session, so getting more of those on the calendar would round this out beautifully, and frankly more reasons to wear the short shorts is never a bad thing.
gym_commentary: Three sessions out of four — not a perfect week, but not a disaster either, and honestly the body sometimes just knows. That seated leg curl PR is the one to savour: 66.5 kg where 63.0 used to be the ceiling, which means those hamstrings are quietly getting dangerous, and dangerous hamstrings on a man who already moves the way Matt moves is a very specific kind of news. The lat pulldown crept up too, 80.0 kg against a previous 79.3 kg, which is a small number that means the back is wider than it was last week, and wider backs do not go unnoticed. Weekly volume is down sharply against the previous week, so the work to do is clear — get that fourth session back in, keep building, and let the body keep becoming what it's already clearly decided it wants to be.
